slice: Local Messenger/Mail/Community draft handoff bus polish
intent: Make built-in Messenger, Mail, and Community feel fully interactive and cohesive by preserving draft context as it is promoted between surfaces, while keeping every action local-only and unwired.
product_direction: Oyatie will build a hyperscaler-grade cloud substrate and dogfood all FD-001 microservices as tenant workloads on that substrate. FD-001 product delivery remains the master-plan product goal; Oyatie Cloud is the substrate that proves the platform can host real production tenants.
implementation_summary: Added a visible Draft Handoff Bus card to the Work Hub context rail for Messenger/Mail/Community source, destination, audience, status, and local persistence state.
Added a local handoff state bus in prototype-interactions.js that preserves selected communication context across Messenger → Mail and Mail → Community transitions.
Thread-to-mail now creates a Mail draft from the current Messenger item, switches surfaces, updates the handoff card, and leaves a local draft in the Mail list.
Publish local/community poll now creates a Community draft from the current Mail/context item, switches surfaces, updates handoff source/destination/audience, and does not send externally.
Queue draft and Clear now update visible handoff/status state so the composer feels functional in the static visual fallback.

before_metrics.issue: Messenger/Mail/Community were individually interactive, but draft context did not visibly persist as an operator promoted a thread to a mail approval brief or a mail brief to a community note.

interaction_assertions: Initial Work Hub shows Messenger active and a Draft Handoff Bus seeded for Messenger → Mail approval brief.
Clicking Promote to Mail / thread-to-mail switches to Mail, prepends a local Mail draft promoted from the Messenger item, updates handoff source/destination/audience, and updates comms status.
Clicking Publish local switches to Community, prepends a local Community draft promoted from Mail, updates handoff state, and keeps publication local-only.
Typing in the composer and clicking Queue draft prepends a local draft, clears the textarea, and updates handoff/status text.
No console or page errors were observed across desktop, tablet, and mobile audits.
responsive_assertions: 1440x1000: Work Hub handoff flow passes and no horizontal page overflow (scrollWidth == innerWidth == 1440).
1024x900: Work Hub handoff flow passes and no horizontal page overflow (scrollWidth == innerWidth == 1024).
390x844: Work Hub handoff flow passes and no horizontal page overflow (scrollWidth == innerWidth == 390).

visual_verdict.category_match: Bominal-inspired professional Work Hub with functional local draft handoffs across Messenger, Mail, and Community, visible provenance, and no external-send boundary.
differences_remaining: The Work Hub is now more behaviorally cohesive, but the full application shell is still a broad mockup rather than a final production product.
Backend delivery, persistence, workflow execution, identity, billing, deployment, and cloud mutation remain intentionally absent.
visual_verdict.reasoning: The slice directly strengthens the user's explicit Messenger/Mail/Community requirement: actions now carry context across surfaces, leave visible local drafts, and update a persistent handoff bus, instead of being isolated buttons.

commands.cmd: podman restart oya-frontend-prototype-live and curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/

known_limits: All Work Hub state is local visual/browser state only; no external message, email, community post, workflow run, IAM, billing, deploy, or cloud mutation occurs.
The active goal remains incomplete/unproven as a whole; this is a verified polish slice toward the complete cohesive Oyatie mockup.
